evidence.source: Hong Kong Educational University, Lexicon of Chinese Phonology: Richi (貴)
evidence.text: The page presents oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and standard forms. Its written explanation describes the forms as hands holding earth and analyzes 貝 as the semantic element and 中 as the phonetic element. This is an account from that reference; its proposed 中 phonetic analysis differs from the traditional 臾 analysis.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 貴

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcribing 說文解字 and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted 說文 entry glosses 貴 as “not cheap” and analyzes it as 从貝臾聲, adding 臾，古文蕢. Duan's annotation gives the fanqie 居胃切. This establishes what the historical dictionary asserts; it does not independently confirm that the early graph depicted the same components.
evidence.title: 說文解字「貴」

evidence.source: Kim Jun-su, Korea Journal of Chinese Linguistics (2016), article record and abstract
evidence.text: The abstract argues 貴 and 遺 have different graphic and phonological origins and says 貴 is 貝 plus 臾, described as the protoform of 簣, as phonetic. It proposes Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese *kluds for 貴 and reports a modified Baxter–Sagart proposal *kut-s. The source presents competing reconstruction-system results; neither is a direct attestation of ancient pronunciation.
evidence.title: 《說文解字》貴聲系字의 上古音 再構에 대한 小考

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary's editorial notes trace several later variant spellings. It treats 䝿 as a direct regularization of the small-seal form and discusses other shapes as graphic variants or possible corruptions. One note explicitly warns that an old form of 蕢 was later misread in some dictionaries as an ancient form of 貴; 說文 itself says 臾 is an ancient form of 蕢. These notes concern later transmitted variants, not proof of the original graph's depiction.
evidence.title: A03945 貴 - 教育部《異體字字典》

gaps: No primary inscription corpus entry was opened to establish the earliest attested spelling or sense of 貴; do not infer that date from dictionary ordering or search-result snippets.
The claimed Warring States phrase 黃金之貴 and the Zuozhuan market-price example remain unverified leads here. Their textual date, manuscript witness, and exact graph usage need primary-source checking.

Early graphic analyses conflict: one opened educational reference describes hands holding earth and calls 貝 semantic, 中 phonetic; 說文 instead gives 貝 semantic and 臾 phonetic. The evidence accessed here does not resolve the original depiction or phonetic component; no glyph image was visually inspected.

The dossier's *kluds is consistent with the opened 2016 paper's Zhengzhang proposal. That paper also reports a different Baxter–Sagart proposal *kut-s. I did not verify the reconstruction from the primary reconstruction publications or establish an uncontested Old Chinese value.

The role of 臾 as a sound component is asserted by 說文 and the 2016 study, but a complete reading-by-reading historical correspondence series for 臾 and 貴 was not independently compiled. Modern Mandarin guì and Cantonese gwai3 are dossier readings, not externally verified here.

The path from “not cheap/high price” to social rank, worth, esteem, or honor is semantically plausible and later dictionaries list such meanings, but dated evidence establishing each extension was not inspected.

The dossier's simplified form 贵 is acknowledged as the current counterpart of 貴, but the exact official adoption record and a dated pre-1956 attestation of this shape were not established in accessible pages.

No independent loanword analysis was found or needed to account for the supported formation claims; the Tibetan comparison in the dossier was not verified and should not be treated as demonstrated etymology.
